subject: Sparrow Health renewal: vendor comparison and performance proof request
messages:
From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@sparrowhealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@sparrowhealth.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion / benchmarking request

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. We're coming up on our renewal window (Aug 1) and the execs have asked for a short vendor comparison so they can justify the platform decision to finance. A competitor (NimbusAI) has proposed an on‑prem pricing model and a hardware migration plan that looks compelling on paper — we need to confirm whether Redwood can match performance and cost for our batch inference workloads.

Could you run a short proof of performance for the specific workload attached (see summary + sample payloads)? We're most concerned about:
- 99th percentile latency for 1–2k concurrent chat sessions
- sustained throughput for nightly embeddings (20k docs)
- token cost per 1M tokens with/without caching

Attachments: sparrow_poc_profile.csv (workload profile), sample_payloads.json

If Redwood can show parity on those metrics AND provide a committed capacity proposal / term concession, we'll push to keep you as our inference partner. Otherwise procurement will run the bakeoff. Can you get preliminary numbers and a proposed save offer by next Friday (5/7)?

Thanks,
Alyssa Greene
Director, Platform Ops
Sparrow Health

From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion / benchmarking request

Folks — forwarding Sparrow's ask. They want a quick PoP + a save offer by 5/7. Internal asks:
- Ben: lead the perf run + produce the 99p latency and throughput numbers on our hosted + dedicated configs. Use the PoC harness linked in the drive.
- Marissa: draft a concise save offer that includes a short term concession (pricing or uplift credits) and a dedicated uplift option. Include an exec meeting invite.
- Sergio: pre-check SOC2/Security docs; Alyssa will want evidence if we get to exec.

I'll coordinate the external reply once we have numbers. Use this mutual action plan (MAP) template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-Sparrow-POC

Rachel Kim
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 11:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion / benchmarking request

Team — I ran an initial harness against Sparrow's sample payloads this morning. Quick notes (hosted vs dedicated candidate):
- 99p latency (hosted, gen-2 model): 210ms (seq len avg 64)
- 99p latency (dedicated, q4 quant, tuned kernels): 130ms
- Nightly embeddings throughput: hosted sustained 18k/docs in 45m; dedicated 22k/docs in 32m
- Token cost delta: dedicated quant path reduces per‑token cost ~28% vs hosted baseline with caching enabled

I attached the raw results CSV and test config. I recommend offering them a limited dedicated commit: 2x dedicated slots with a 6‑month uplift credit (to offset migration), and a 12‑month term at a discounted per‑token rate. That gives them predictable throughput and a cost match vs Nimbus on busy windows.

Proposed quick save offer (high level):
- 12 month term, dedicated capacity pool (2 slots), 20% off hosted list with quant path enabled
- 3 months of credits equal to first‑month committed spend
- Priority migration assistance and extended support SLA (4hr P1)

Attachments: sparrow_poc_results.csv, perf_config.yaml

Ben Carter
Director of Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Greene <alyssa@sparrowhealth.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@vcpartners.com>, procurement@sparrowhealth.com
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Sparrow Health renewal — preliminary save proposal and next steps

Hi Alyssa — great talking through this. Attached is a concise save proposal plus a mutual action plan that maps milestones (PoP verification, legal redlines, exec review). High level summary:
- Performance: our dedicated config demonstrably meets your 99p latency and exceeds nightly embedding throughput in our test harness (see summary table).
- Commercial: 12‑month term, dedicated pool (2 GPUs equivalent), 20% reduction vs hosted list for quantized path, and a 3‑month credit equal to first‑month committed spend.
- Commitments: migration assistance, prioritized support, and a 30‑day rollback clause if production metrics diverge >10%.

Next actions:
1) Can you confirm availability for a 30‑minute exec tech call next week (options: Tue 5/11 10am PT / Wed 5/12 9am PT)?
2) Loop in procurement contact for contract redlines — we can send a short form amendment to your current agreement.
3) Sergio will share SOC2 + encryption KMS attestation once you confirm the exec call.

Attachments: redwood_save_offer_v1.pdf, mutual_action_plan_sparrow.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
